note: Depth modules at the level of job titles in postings. They do not create new axes: `core_ref` points to the Core's technical domains and role functions. ME_V3_2 brought the number to eight: equipment and maintenance was added, quality and reliability was separated from test and verification, and analysis/prediction and exploration/advanced development, which had pointed to the same role function, were split apart. Role functions and role packs are paired one-to-one. `differs_from` states in one line how a role differs from its neighbors, and the report reads that line. Items ask about a different judgment for each role: running the same question with only the role name changed would make comparison meaningless.

exploration.note: All eight roles can be compared. Rather than asking fifty-six items at once, you pick up to two roles of interest after the Core in-depth part, and the chosen roles are examined in depth from STANDARD up. Roles you did not pick are compared through the axes confirmed in the Core. Choosing a role does not change the Core judgment.

packs.owns: Finalizes shape, dimensions, material and tolerances

differs_from.line: Analysis is responsible for the validity of the prediction; design has the authority to change drawing dimensions
Production engineering sets the conditions for making it repeatedly; design decides what is made in the first place

items.ask: Have you set dimensions or tolerances yourself, with the authority to change them?
Have you delivered drawings and a parts list that went to fabrication?
When requirements conflicted, have you decided which one to protect first?
Have you calculated a tolerance stack-up to confirm that parts would assemble?
Have you corrected dimensions after running into an assembly or breakage problem?
Have you chosen the material and grade yourself?
Has your design been adopted at a design review and built as it was?

application_material: A set of assembly and part drawings
One page explaining where you concentrated the tolerance budget

packs.owns: Predicts results before anything is built and is responsible for the validity of that prediction
decides: Property values to use and their sources

differs_from.line: Design has the authority to change dimensions; analysis provides the evidence for why they should change
Exploration creates a method when none exists; analysis establishes validity with existing methods

items.ask: Have you set the constraints and load application points yourself?
Have you changed the mesh to check that the results converge?
Have you checked analysis values against test values and written down why they differed?
Have you documented the analysis conditions and assumptions?
Have you estimated the magnitude of analysis results with a hand calculation?
Has a design change been approved based on your analysis?
When results looked wrong, have you fixed the conditions or model and run it again?

application_material: A table comparing analysis with test results
One page listing conditions and assumptions

packs.owns: Establishes the functions to deliver and the methods to use when no specification exists
decides: Scope of the problem to tackle

differs_from.line: Analysis establishes the validity of predictions with existing methods; exploration creates a method when none is available
Design delivers a solution that meets a given specification; exploration writes that specification in the first place

items.ask: Have you created a new method because no usable one existed?
Have you narrowed down and settled on the problem to tackle yourself?
Have you set out assumptions to verify and checked those first?
Have you decided which requirements to give up and narrowed the scope?
Have you confirmed that something would not work and changed direction?
Have you published your method and conditions so others could reproduce your results?
Have your results become the starting point for the next stage of development?

application_material: A full record of how a method was established
A table of assumptions and verification results
One page on what did not work and why

packs.owns: Measures whether what was built meets the requirements and makes the call

differs_from.line: Testing judges a single case; quality assures that requirements hold through mass production and over the product's life
Analysis predicts before anything is built; testing judges what has been built

items.ask: Have you written down pass/fail criteria in advance?
Have you built a fixture that applies loads or constraints like real use?
Have you delivered a test report all the way to the verdict?
Have you measured several times to check the spread?
When values fluctuated, have you changed the measurement method or fixture?
Have you measured vibration or noise and separated where it was coming from?
Has a shipping or design change decision been made based on your verdict?

application_material: One page on variation and uncertainty

packs.owns: Sets the methods and conditions so the same thing can be made repeatedly

differs_from.line: Design decides what is made; production engineering sets the conditions for making it repeatedly
Production engineering decides what to make on that equipment and under which conditions; maintenance keeps the equipment running

items.ask: Have you chosen the manufacturing method and machining sequence yourself?
Have you set the range of conditions through trial machining?
Have you delivered a work standard or process chart?
Have you compared target yield or process time with the actual figures?
When defects occurred, have you changed the conditions or tooling?
Have you asked for a design change based on how easy it would be to manufacture?
Has production run on conditions you set?

application_material: A record of how the range of conditions was set

packs.owns: Keeps the equipment performing as it should, and brings it back when it stops

differs_from.line: Maintenance keeps the equipment running; production engineering decides what to make on it and under which conditions
Testing judges the product; maintenance is responsible for the condition of the equipment that makes that judgment

items.ask: Have you set inspection items or intervals yourself?
Have you judged warning signs from noise, heat and vibration?
When the same symptom came back, have you split the cause into equipment, conditions and the way it was used?
Have you checked equipment condition with calibration references or reference samples?
Have you left inspection checklists or action records that others could follow?
Have you decided how many spare parts or consumables to keep?
Have you taught others how to use equipment and handed it over?

packs.owns: Assures, through criteria and judgments, that requirements hold through mass production and over the product's life

differs_from.line: Testing judges a single case; quality assures the whole of mass production and service life
Production engineering sets the conditions; quality checks against criteria that those conditions are held

items.ask: Have you worked out what is most critical under the customer's operating conditions and decided what to control?
Have you set the items to control and their control ranges yourself?
Have you calculated process capability indices to see whether a process was in control?
Have you confirmed service life with accelerated or repeated testing?
When the same defect came back, have you separated occurrence from escape and set countermeasures?
Have you combined the cause, countermeasures and verification results into one report and had it approved?
Has a process or inspection changed because of your criteria?

application_material: One page on the basis for a life estimate

packs.owns: Ties together many people's requirements, schedules and constraints and sets the order of decisions

differs_from.line: Design finalizes one part; technical planning sets the order so that many parts fit together
Quality checks whether criteria are met; technical planning decides who meets those criteria and when

items.ask: Have you gathered requirements from several people into one table and found where they conflict?
Have you attached to each requirement what would count as meeting it?
Have you decided what had to be matched between parts or teams?
Have you traced the impact of a changed requirement and rebuilt the schedule?
Have you kept a requirements table and change history?
At the end of a project, have you opened the requirements table and picked out the items that were missed?
Has your team worked to a schedule and division of work you set?

application_material: One page summarizing roles and interfaces
